sections.html:
Attleboro, in Bristol County, borders Rhode Island. Its 2020 population of 46,461 is a record high, and it has 19,097 housing units, 4.4 percent of them vacant. The Providence area is its main orbit, with ties to Boston too.

Listings usually name the village, because the city is a patchwork of older mill villages and crossroads: City Center beside the L.G. Balfour Riverwalk, South Attleboro near the state line, West and East Attleboro, Hebronville, Dodgeville, Maple Square, Briggs Corner, North Corner, Oak Hill, Park Square, East Junction and Camp Hebron.

The city has been settled since 1634, so houses range widely in age. Heating systems, wiring and roofs deserve a careful look before you set price expectations.

Interstate 95 enters the state between Attleboro and Pawtucket, and Interstate 295 ends nearby. Two MBTA commuter rail stops exist, one downtown and one in South Attleboro. GATRA buses link Attleboro, Taunton and surrounding towns.

A house near a rail station or an I-95 ramp appeals to people commuting toward Providence or Boston. Mention that if it applies to yours.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Four installments are due each year: August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. Any date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next Monday. The collector's real estate tax page flags several rules that trip people up.

  • Interest on late amounts builds daily, at 14 percent per year.
  • The city will not accept a postmark as proof of on-time payment.
  • A bill lost in the mail is no excuse for skipping the tax or the interest.
  • Ways to pay: online, by phone, by mail, at City Hall, 77 Park Street, or in the Pine Street entrance drop box.

Sections on municipal lien certificates and tax title sit on that same page. Read them first if you owe a balance and want to sell.

sections.h2: Who receives the bill after a sale
sections.html:
The bill follows the owner of record on January 1 of the assessment year. A buyer may wait a while before a bill shows their name, and the city urges new owners to check their details with the Assessor's Office.

As the seller, never assume a later bill will reach the buyer. Settle the tax on the closing statement.

The Assessor's Office, 77 Park Street, posts this calendar on its key dates page.

DateWhat happens
July 1First day of the fiscal year, and the qualification date for personal exemptions
December 1Deadline to apply for farm, recreational or forest classification
January 1Assessment date for the following fiscal year
February 1Deadline to apply for a property tax abatement
April 1Deadline to apply for personal exemptions
June 30End of the fiscal year

A denied abatement can be appealed. The state's Appellate Tax Board guide sets a three-month window for that step.

Unpaid tax puts a lien on the house right away, and a taking may follow. As the Land Court's overview describes it, 30 days of nonpayment can bring a demand, and a taking can be recorded 14 days after the demand. Paying every dollar owed redeems the property any time before a foreclosure judgment.

If you sell in that window, the sale proceeds cover the balance. With interest running daily at 14 percent per year, each week of delay adds to the payoff.

Any sale of a one or two family home calls for a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate of compliance. The Department of Fire Services guide says to phone the local fire department right after a closing date is set. Battery smoke alarms past 10 years or expired need replacing, and the inspection carries a fee.

Attleboro deeds are recorded at the Bristol County Registry of Deeds. A link on the Assessor's page leads to deed searches, handy for confirming how your name is spelled on record.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with taxes owed
sections.html:
1. Ask the collector for your total, including daily interest on any late amount.
  2. Request a municipal lien certificate to give your attorney a firm number.
  3. Check with the Assessor's Office that the owner details match your deed.
  4. Book the alarm inspection as soon as the closing date is fixed.
  5. At the table, the attorney settles the balance from your proceeds.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Attleboro houses as-is. Tax debt, postponed repairs or an estate need not stop a sale, and the payoff happens at closing.

Most of the waiting in an Attleboro sale comes from the offices, not the buyer. Bills fall on quarterly dates, so ask the collector early which installment is next and whether you will owe it before closing. The fire department will not book the alarm inspection until you have a closing date, so line that up the same day the date is set.

If you are behind, the timing is tighter. After 30 days of nonpayment the city can send a demand, and 14 days after that it can record a taking. A buyer who can close on a date you choose gives you room to pay everything before that point.

Cash Home Buyers works from the closing date you need. We purchase as-is, so there are no repair requests to negotiate, and the lien certificate, payoff and deed recording are handled through closing with your attorney.

sections.h2: What to gather before you call
sections.html:
Pull together your most recent bill, the loan statement if a mortgage remains, and any letter from the city about overdue amounts. If a relative owned the house before you, have the deed information handy, since the owner of record on January 1 decides who receives the bill.

Then make two calls. The collector can tell you the balance and the interest to date. The Assessor's Office can confirm the owner details on file and tell you whether an abatement application is open. Keep notes with names and dates. If you are weighing an abatement, remember the February 1 deadline and that you should keep paying while it is decided.

Finally, if the house has been vacant or needs major work, tell any buyer up front. A cash buyer expects to see a house in rough shape, while a lender-financed buyer may walk away after the inspection.

sections.h2: Listing, selling on your own, or a cash offer
sections.html:
Every route gives something up. Which one you give up depends on your priorities.

List the house and a well-kept property may sell for more, though you take on showings and negotiation. Sell without an agent and you skip a commission, yet marketing and paperwork land on you. A direct cash offer suits a house that needs work, an estate sale, or anyone who wants a closing date they can count on. Judge offers by the money in your hand after taxes, payoffs and repairs, not the headline price.

faqs.q: How many people live in Attleboro, Massachusetts?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 46,461 residents, the highest count in the city's history.

faqs.q: When are Attleboro property taxes due?
faqs.a: August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, payment is due the following Monday.

faqs.q: Does Attleboro accept postmarks for tax payments?
faqs.a: No. Payment has to be received by the due date, and late amounts accrue interest daily at 14 percent per year.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for an Attleboro abatement application?
faqs.a: February 1. The Assessor's Office lists it as the deadline to apply for a property tax abatement.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Attleboro house with taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes and liens are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so request a written payoff figure from the collector before your closing date.
